sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU. Part II Phonology and grammar of Abelam (Wosera dialect), sec. 4.22 p.27 and sec. 5.2 'Stress' pp.29-30.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: NEIGHBOUR ONLY: 'Stress is non-phonemic, being wholly conditioned by the syllable and nuclear structure of the phrase'; primary stress on the higher-ranking nucleus of the first two nuclei of the phonological phrase (ties: first, unless the 2nd syllable is closed or the phrase exceeds two syllables), phrase-final open syllable always unstressed, secondary stress on adjacent equal-rank nuclei. But sec. 4.22: the Wosera material was recorded Feb 1960 at Kunjingini mission (3°46'S 143°2'E), informants from Kunjingini No.1 and Abusit = the Kamu-Kundi Wosera dialect of Abelam (Ambulas, ambu1247),…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid hang1263 Hanga Hundi (page and JSON record); reference 97333.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic: only descriptive source is Wendel 1993 (grammar); other refs Aikhenvald 2015 and Laycock 1965 (subclassification), Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment). Alt names Kwasengen, West Wosera. No SIL OPD entry in Glottolog.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Reproduces the consonant and vowel tables from 'Anonyme, 2011, Hanga Hundi Organised phonology Data, manuscrit, Ukarumpa, SIL International' (p.1, p.3) and gives its sil.org reapdata URL; says nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 2008. The Manambu language of East Sepik, Papua New Guinea. Oxford: OUP. Ch. 1, sec. 1.5, p.21.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identity only: 'West Wosera (including Hanga Kundi, Kwasengen, Pukago, Banwingei). Wendel (1993: 1-5) argues that West Wosera is a separate language group. However, this may well be a continuum of dialects.. (Wilson 1976, 1980; Manabe 1981).' No stress statement for Hanga Hundi.

sources.note: Only names Kwasengen (Nungwaia speakers are 'Kwasengen according to Wurm and Hattori 1981: Map 6'); nothing on its stress.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, language hang1263, inventory PH 1064 'Hanga Hundi; Kwasengen; West Wosera' (23 segments), source Wendel 1993.
sources.note: Segment inventory only; nothing on stress, tone or suprasegmentals. Confirms Wendel 1993 contains a phoneme inventory.

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Hanga Hundi (wals_code_hhu), source Wendel 1993; datapoint pages for chapters 14A-17A (Goedemans & van der Hulst, stress).
